commands.author: baanish

target.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt-cache continuity breaks across room events and native Responses
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Long-lived embedded sessions lose prompt-cache continuity across ambient group `room_event` turns, queued/compaction paths, and native `openai-chatgpt-responses` continuation.

The original reproduction used:

```json
{
  "messages": {
    "groupChat": {
      "visibleReplies": "automatic",
      "unmentionedInbound": "room_event"
    }
  }
}
```

Unmentioned group messages correctly become strict `message_tool_only` room events. The bug is that this turn-specific delivery mode also changes cache-visible prompt/tool state inside the same session. Further investigation found that the stable mode was dropped in queued and compaction paths, while built-in authenticated ChatGPT Responses sessions were misclassified as custom streams and bypassed native continuation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.6.11 with the configuration above.
2. In one Discord group/channel session, trigger an initial mentioned or session-start turn.
3. Send unmentioned messages in the same session so they arrive as `room_event` turns.
4. Exercise a queued turn or compaction in the same session.
5. Compare serialized provider requests, generated prompt/tool digests, and provider cache metrics.
6. On native GPT-5.5 or GPT-5.6 with `openai-chatgpt-responses`, inspect whether the second turn uses `previous_response_id` plus delta-only input or replays full context.

### Expected behavior

- Effective room-event delivery may remain strict `message_tool_only`.
- The cached prompt/tool contract should remain session-stable across ordinary, room-event, queued, memory-flush, and compaction turns.
- Executable `message` tools must still receive the real turn mode so targetless sends retain the internal source-reply sink and best-effort behavior.
- Built-in authenticated ChatGPT Responses sessions should reach native continuation; custom streams should retain their existing routing.

### Actual behavior

The original same-session traces showed:

| turn | kind | prompt tokens | cached tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | session start | 46,540 | 0 |
| 2 | room_event | 46,826 | 9,856 |
| 3 | room_event | 47,590 | 2,048 |
| 4 | room_event | 48,660 | 47,616 |

The generated system prompt changed from 106,647 chars (SHA prefix `151fdb3fb5b43caa`) to 105,986 chars (SHA prefix `62b9313a931f656b`). The first divergent region switched automatic final-reply guidance to `message(action=send)`, and tool inventory also changed between 44 and 47 tools.

Additional source-level failures found during investigation:

- queued and compaction entry points rebuilt from the effective turn mode instead of the stable prompt-facing mode;
- executable message tools temporarily inherited the prompt mode, which could disable room-event source-reply sink behavior;
- Codex reusable thread instructions could contradict actual room-event delivery;
- the built-in authenticated session stream lacked an identity marker, so normal embedded routing bypassed native WebSocket continuation.

### Resolution under review

PR #102189, current head `f0d85b0829d54ec9f3bda3406168f8bf2d8c0d6d`, now:

- separates actual delivery from cache-visible prompt/tool shape;
- preserves the actual mode in executable Pi and Codex message tools;
- propagates the stable mode through primary, queued, memory-flush, and every compaction path;
- keeps Codex thread instructions stable while applying strict delivery guidance per turn;
- routes only OpenClaw's marked built-in authenticated stream to native Responses continuation;
- proves GPT-5.6 continuation with `previous_response_id` and delta-only second-turn input.

Post-fix live traces reached roughly 49k-52k cached tokens on approximately 51k-55k context. The exact PR head is installed locally and healthy. All GitHub checks pass; ClawSweeper rates it platinum with diamond proof and reports no contributor-facing line-level blocker.

### Compatibility decision

To keep ambient room-event prompt/tool shape stable across sender changes, the PR uses the safe non-owner owner-only core-tool inventory for every ambient room event. Owner-only tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`, and `computer` are not prompt-visible on those turns. Runtime authorization remains enforced.

Maintainers must decide whether to accept that cache-stable ambient-room compatibility contract or request a different owner-tool policy.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.6.11
- Initial reproduction model: Synthetic GLM-5.2 through an OpenAI-compatible proxy
- Native continuation reproduction: GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 via `openai-chatgpt-responses`
- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Install: CLI/gateway LaunchAgent

Raw traces are omitted because they contain private user, channel, account, and credential-adjacent metadata. All evidence above is sanitized.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were removed.
